texts.orig: An important different lies in the nature of the par ent compound. In the cuprates the half-filled system is an insulator which is usually considered a Mott insulator; testifying the central role of electron correlations (Even if it has been recently proposed that the degree of correlation can be smaller than usually believed[2]) . The undoped pnictides are instead still metallic,  despite the magnetic ordering, suggesting weaker degree of electronic correlations _ The actual strength of correlation in pnictides is lively debated: while there is no obvious reason to invoke correlation as the player in the game as it happens in cuprates; it has been proposed that these compounds are actually close to Mott transition[3] . key

texts.orig: Another  peculiarity of pnictides is that; according to density-functional theory calculations; all the five d-bands of iron are relevant as opposed to the single copper band of the cuprates. Multiple bands crossthe Fermi level are confirmed by angular resolved photoemission. The relevance of multiband effects can solve the discrepancy between different estimates of the role of correlations. Indeed electron correlation can induce a much richer physics in multiband systems with respect to single band. In particular, different   bands can be affected differently by correlations; and even tually one can have an orbital-selective Mott transi tion (OSMT), in which   some bands   become insulatand others are metallic. Signatures of an orbitalselective behavior have been detected by angle-resolved ing ing
